turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello. Well... I guess I'm here because of church. 

The folks there... they said I was doing some odd things lately. Like at the potluck table. I guess I was just... standing there, holding the serving spoon up in the air. Just not moving. And... folding the same stack of napkins over and over again, while people were waiting on me. 

So... I don't know. That's why I came.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes standing still holding a spoon without moving and repetitively folding napkins, which are examples of disorganized or abnormal motor behavior (posturing, catalepsy, stereotypy).

turns.doctor_question: When you were standing there holding the spoon or folding the napkins, could you hear people talking to you or were you aware of what was happening around you?
turns.patient_response: I... well, I'm not too sure. I guess I just wasn't paying mind to much of anything right then. They said they were talking to me, but... I don't really remember hearing it.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing any voices or seeing things that other people around you do not seem to notice?
turns.patient_response: No... I don't think so. I haven't heard anything like that. Just... regular things, I guess.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or seeing things that others do not notice.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any known medical conditions or have you recently taken any new medications or substances?
turns.patient_response: No... I don't think so. I ain't taking no new pills or nothing. Just... been the same as always, I suppose.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed yourself repeating the words or movements of other people without meaning to?
turns.patient_response: No... I ain't noticed doing nothing like that. I don't think so, anyway.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient explicitly denies repeating the words or movements of other people, which corresponds to echolalia and echopraxia.

turns.doctor_question: When people at church asked you to do something, like move along or put the spoon down, did you find yourself intentionally doing the opposite of what they asked?
turns.patient_response: No... I wasn't doing that. I was just... doing what I was doing. I didn't mean to do the opposite or nothing.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient explicitly denies intentionally doing the opposite of what was asked, which rules out the negativism subtype of disorganized/abnormal behavior.

turns.doctor_question: During these times when you seem stuck or unresponsive, are you able to speak if you try, or do you find that you are completely unable to say anything at all?
turns.patient_response: I don't... I reckon I can speak if I need to. I ain't completely unable or nothing like that. Just... sometimes I just don't have nothing to say. I don't really know about being stuck.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient explicitly denies being unable to speak (mutism) and denies feeling 'stuck' (stupor), which are subtypes of disorganized or abnormal motor behavior.

turns.doctor_question: When you are speaking with others, do you find that your thoughts get jumbled or that you have trouble keeping track of what you are trying to say?
turns.patient_response: Well... I guess sometimes. Like if the ladies ask me about blankets, or... choir practice. I mean to answer straight. But... I don't know, my words just run off on me. I end up talking about beans... or hymns, or my roses. Then folks just look at me... like they can't find what I'm saying. I don't really know why.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient confirms that their words 'run off' and they jump between unrelated topics like beans, hymns, and roses, making it hard for others to understand them, which indicates disorganized thinking and speech.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me what day of the week it is today, and where exactly we are right now?
turns.patient_response: I... I ain't rightly sure what day it's gotten to be. I don't keep track so much. And we're... well, we're just here. In this office. I don't know much more than that.
